widgets_values:
INTERIOR V2V — keep both ends, regenerate the middle

WHAT IS BEING TESTED
  Every seam we have measured had a pinned PAST and an open future, and
  the failure is always the same: the model reproduces the handed-over
  prefix, then makes a fresh decision. Feathering, partial strength,
  whole-clip gradients and sigma-release all came back null over nine
  rounds. Three later attempts at sharing context between neighbours
  (drift control, the halo, the window margin) failed too.

  Every one of those gave the model more context about where it CAME
  FROM. None gave it anywhere to ARRIVE. H3 Latent Bracket does: the
  last steps are stamped back at every denoise step, so the clip cannot
  end anywhere except where the source ends.

  That is structurally unlike everything in the failed pile. It is not a
  prediction that it works.

HOW IT IS WIRED
  H3 Encode AV encodes the source; the conditioning node makes a fresh
  target latent of the same shape; the bracket copies the source's first
  51 and last 51 frames into it and sets their noise mask to 0. The
  sampler runs at FULL denoise — the middle is new content, not a
  restyle, so there is no Split Sigmas here.

  192 frames (17*11+5). 51 held at each end is 15 latent steps each;
  90 frames generated in between. 51 is also a multiple of 3, so both
  brackets land on exact 40 Hz audio ticks.

WHAT TO EXPECT, HONESTLY
  TWO temporal mask edges, and no setting has ever softened one. If the
  middle reads as bracketed by cuts, that is the known failure and not a
  surprise. The interesting part is the CONTENT between them — whether a
  model with a fixed destination drifts the way an open-ended one does.

THE PROMPT DESCRIBES AN ERRAND
  Something that leaves and returns. A middle that ends somewhere else
  is asking the bracket to force a discontinuity it cannot hide.

widgets_values_named.text:
PDD UPSCALE PASS — second pass over a finished render.

INPUT is a clip you already made (node 1). This does not generate.

THE CHAIN
  VHS_LoadVideo -> H3EncodeAV -> SamplerCustomAdvanced -> decode

H3EncodeAV
  Encodes the clip into an H3 video+audio latent AND owns the
  resize, so its width/height/length outputs drive the H3
  conditioning node. One number, one place — the latent's shape
  IS the render size, so a separate resize node could disagree
  with it and the failure would be silent.

  megapixels 2.87 -> ~1280x2240 on your aspect, 2x linear.
  pin_audio ON -> the source soundtrack is held through
  sampling, so a video pass cannot resample your dialogue.
  Frame count trims DOWN to 17n+5; the info output says by how
  much, because losing frames off a take silently is the kind of
  thing that gets blamed on the model.

SAMPLING
  PDD sigmas -> SplitSigmasDenoise -> low_sigmas -> sampler.
  Every sigma PDD emits is a block boundary, so the truncated
  schedule still lands on the grid its heads were fused for. A
  normal scheduler cut to 5 steps does not. euler, because the
  fusion plan assumes a first-order deterministic solver.

ABOVE THE CANVAS, ON PURPOSE
  H3 generates at 1.03 MP (768x1344). At 2.87 MP you are 2.8x
  past it. That duplicates features when generating FROM NOISE;
  at low denoise the structure is already there and only RoPE
  positions extrapolate, which degrades softly. Finding where it
  actually breaks is the point of this graph.

THE LADDER (megapixels on H3EncodeAV)
  1.03 -> 768x1344   at canvas, safest
  1.84 -> 1024x1792  1.6x
  2.87 -> 1280x2240  2x, this default
  Cost is QUADRATIC in area: 2.87 MP is ~8x the attention of 1.03.

BYPASSED, kept only so the graph's history is readable: the SAM3
chain, H3MatchSource, H3SubjectCrop/Uncrop and H3MaskInpaint. The
crop node was cropping nothing and the mask was pinning nothing —
they were how this encoded a latent before H3EncodeAV existed.

SIGMA SHIFT MUST BE 12.0
  The PDD file was fused at shift_video 12.0, and BOTH the fused
  heads and the sigmas this node emits are functions of the shift.
  At any other value the sampler steps one curve while the model
  integrates another. The node refuses rather than letting it
  render something merely wrong.
  H3 08, which this was copied from, ran 3.0 — if that was a
  deliberate choice for refines, PDD costs you it.

CONTEXT WINDOWS
  90-frame windows, 39 overlap, pyramid fuse. Windowing is the
  right tool for a REFINE: chunking exists to make separately
  GENERATED segments continue each other, and here nothing needs
  continuing — the motion and composition are already in the
  latent and each window only adds local detail.

  absolute_window_positions ON and causal_window_fix OFF. Without
  the first, every window thinks it sits at the clip origin and
  renders the opening of the shot; the overlaps then crossfade
  between two openings, which is the flicker.

  IT ONLY CUTS THE TEMPORAL AXIS. The 80x140 spatial grid is per
  latent frame either way, so this lets a LONG clip fit at 2x —
  it cannot rescue a single window that is too big on its own.
  If one 90-frame window still OOMs, drop megapixels, not frames.

THE TILING WIDGETS DO NOTHING — corrected 2026-09-03
  H3EncodeAV's temporal_size/overlap and VAEDecodeTiled's settings
  are inert. H3's VAE sets handles_tiling, so encode_tiled routes to
  the model's own method, and that method is `return self.encode(x)`
  with every tile argument swallowed by **kwargs.

  The VAE always chunks temporally at clip_length = 17 frames. So a
  long clip was NEVER one giant call — the chunking was happening all
  along, which is why 30 seconds fits. An earlier version of this note
  claimed these widgets capped peak memory. They never did.

  Windowing on the SAMPLER is real and does what it says. Only the VAE
  tiling controls are decorative.

  encode_temporal slices those 17-frame blocks disjointly and
  concatenates: no overlap, no blend. Spatial tiling DOES blend (a
  linear crossfade on the x and y axes); temporal does not. 17 is the
  model's native block — 17n+5 pixel frames to 5n+2 latent frames —
  so whether that boundary is a seam or simply the architecture is an
  OPEN QUESTION. If a long decode ever shows periodic structure at
  ~0.7s intervals, that is where to look.

nodes.title: ③ RESULT — who replaces her; <Video 1> supplies the pose
widgets_values: Hand-inked comic book animation. Heavy black linework, flat cel shading, bold halftone texture, saturated ink colours, visible drawn outlines on every edge.

The same shot redrawn as hand-inked comic animation. Identical framing, identical camera, identical motion, identical staging -- every subject stays exactly where they are doing exactly what they are already doing. Only the RENDERING changes: flat inked colour instead of photographic light, drawn outlines instead of photographic edges, halftone instead of film grain.
Do not reinterpret the scene, the location, the framing or the bodies. Change only how it is DRAWN.

widgets_values_named.style: Realistic video. The same shot, unchanged.
widgets_values_named.shots: The same shot as the source, at higher resolution. Identical framing, identical camera, identical motion, identical lighting and colour. Every subject stays exactly where they are, doing exactly what they are already doing, with the same anatomy, the same proportions and the same clothing or lack of it. Nothing enters or leaves the frame. Resolve existing detail and texture only — skin, hair, fabric, edges — and invent nothing.
widgets_values_named.extra_direction: Do not reinterpret the scene, the location, the framing or the bodies. This is a resolution pass over footage that already exists.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values:
RESTYLE = PARTIAL DENOISE. Not a guide clip.

H3 33 fed the whole source in as a guide clip on
AddGuide at full denoise. That does not restyle -- it
RECONSTRUCTS. The guide sits at the target's own time
coordinates and the model treats it as ground truth,
so the output came back as the source. Loosening it
with H3GuideStrength to 0.5, with two style LoRAs at
1.0, changed nothing visible. Measured 2026-09-09.

This is the mechanism that works, and it is the one
H3 24 already used: encode the source INTO the latent,
then denoise only part of the way. What is destroyed
gets redrawn under the prompt and the LoRA; what
survives holds the structure.

SplitSigmasDenoise is the dial:

  0.2   what 24 used -- resolves detail, no restyle
  0.5   <-- set now
  0.65  stronger style, structure starts moving
  0.8   expect the scene to drift

It splits an existing sigma schedule rather than
rebuilding one, so it avoids the int(steps/denoise)
quantisation that makes BasicScheduler's denoise
widget coarse at low step counts.

Audio is pinned by H3EncodeAV itself (pin_audio), so
the soundtrack cannot be resampled by a video pass.

UNTESTED at any value other than 24's 0.2.
